game: Week 5 2025 NYG@NO New York Giants at New Orleans Saints, kickoff 2025-10-05 13:00 ET, dome, spread NO -1.5, total 41.5, implied NO 21.5 / NYG 20.0

script.base: Close dome game, not a shootout. NO -1.5 and a 41.5 total put the Saints at 21.5 and the Giants at 20.0, so the book expects a one-score game with both offenses in the low 20s. Base flow: neither team pulls away by halftime, pace stays modest, and both lean on the lead back rather than a 30-attempt air raid. New Orleans stays with Alvin Kamara (54 carries, 211 rush yards in weeks 2-4, about 18 carries and 70 rush yards a game) and Spencer Rattler. New York stays with Cam Skattebo (46 carries, 184 rush yards, plus 13 targets and 86 receiving yards over those same three games) because Tyrone Tracy Jr. is Doubtful. Malik Nabers (23 targets, 433 air yards) and Chris Olave (30 targets, only 131 yards) are involved, but the 41.5 number does not require either to post a ceiling day.
script.flip1: Saints get up early, run the clock, and Kamara's carries rise while Giants rush attempts die. Skattebo's pure rush line would stall the way a trailing back's does; his rush-plus-receiving line only survives if Dart, who has been worse vs the blitz (EPA/dropback -0.19 blitzed vs -0.05 not blitzed), checks down. Dart also has 12 carries for 54 yards in weeks 2-4, so some scramble yards never reach Skattebo.
script.flip2: Giants score first and New Orleans trails. Ruiz is already Out and Penning and Radunz are Questionable, so a pass-rate spike plus a battered line cuts Kamara's carries toward Kendre Miller (23 carries, 100 yards in weeks 2-4) and Rattler (12 carries, 73 yards). Skattebo's rush volume would rise in that flip. A third, lesser flip is a defensive slog under 41.5 that caps both yardage lines even if the carries are there.

matchup.shell: No middle-of-field open/closed chart and no man/zone rate in the pack, so shell is a proxy from location splits and blitz only. Saints coverage YPA: left 6.54 on 46 throws, middle 10.09 on 23 throws, right 8.56 on 41 throws. Giants coverage YPA: left 7.04 on 53, middle 6.50 on 30, right 5.88 on 77. Saints blitz 35 percent. Giants blitz 39 percent. The Saints bleed is the middle, not the outside corner. The Giants bleed is the run, not a single passing zone.
matchup.pressure: Saints blitz 35 percent and Giants EPA per dropback is -0.19 when blitzed versus -0.05 when not, so pressure should speed Dart up, cut Nabers' deep conversion (433 air yards, only 200 receiving yards on 23 targets in weeks 2-4), and lift checkdowns to Skattebo (2 air yards on 13 targets) and Theo Johnson. Giants blitz 39 percent and Saints EPA per dropback is +0.10 when blitzed versus -0.14 when not, so Rattler has been better against pressure than against a standard rush. Chase Young being Out makes that Giants blitz less likely to wreck Kamara's pass-protection day, but it does not fix the Saints offensive line injuries.
matchup.bleeds: Giants run defense is the loud number on the slate: 6.51 yards per carry and 18 runs of 10-plus yards in four games, with only 10 passes of 20-plus for 170 yards. Saints run defense is not a bleed: 4.34 yards per carry and 14 runs of 10-plus. Saints pass defense bleeds the middle at 10.09 YPA on 23 attempts and has allowed 11 passes of 20-plus for 121 yards. Giants pass defense is tighter on the right (5.88) than the left (7.04).
matchup.overlap: The primary-target overlap the market is not fully showing in this pack is Kamara's carry role into the Giants' 6.51 YPC run defense, with Flannigan-Fowles already Out and Lawrence Questionable. The second overlap is Skattebo's checkdown role into a Saints blitz that Giants have played poorly, plus a Saints front missing Young and Ridgeway. Nabers is the Giants' target leader, but an 18.8-yard average depth of target does not attack the Saints' middle bleed, and his last two listed games are 13 and 20 yards against a 45.5 line. Theo Johnson (12 targets, 61 yards, 87 air yards in weeks 2-4) does attack that middle, but 13.5 receiving yards is a one-quiet-drive number (last four 5, 34, 10, 17) and is not one of the two legs.

pre_mortem: It is Monday and both legs lost. Kamara finished under 57.5 because Ruiz was out, Penning and Radunz never got right, and the Saints run game lived at his recent 3.91 yards per carry instead of the Giants' 6.51 allowed. Miller's 65-yard form showed up again, Lawrence played through the illness tag, and the 6.51 was a previous-opponent number rather than today's front. The 42- and 45-yard games on Kamara's card were the template, not the 99. Skattebo finished under 74.5 rush-plus-receiving because Tracy was active on a snap count, Singletary took the passing-down work, the Saints' 4.34 yards-per-carry defense stuffed early downs even without Chase Young and John Ridgeway, and Dart's air-yard diet to Nabers (433 air yards on 23 targets in weeks 2-4) never checked down. The 59-yard rush-plus-receiving week was the template, not the 121. If the human reads the Saints offensive-line report as stronger than the Giants' run-defense number, Kamara is the leg to cut. It stays on the card only because the skill says a strong read that the data splits on gets flagged, not deleted.
